content:
Jay Chen: filing follow-up from the external pen test — they reported the ability to enumerate KMS key aliases via an internal API. repro steps below, pls advise on severity and remediation.
Sara Patel: can you paste the exact curl / payload you used so we can repro locally?
Jay Chen: sure — ran from a low-priv machine account.
```
export TOKEN=redacted_token
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  https://api.redwood-internal.com/v1/keys?aliasSearch=true
```
returned a JSON list of aliases (no key material) and headers showing route: proxy-prod-01 -> control-plane.
Maya Rivera: that's not supposed to be routable from prod. which env was this executed against (prod/staging)?
Jay Chen: prod. vendor said they used a machine user created via our onboarding flow with minimal scopes.
Ben Morales: hmm. if it's just aliases, the immediate data-exfil risk is lower, but alias enumeration can aid targeted attacks. did you see any missing audit events?
Jay Chen: yes — lookup calls didn't produce `kms.key.lookup` events in the audit stream for the 10:12-10:18 window. I've attached the raw trace in the S3 bucket we gave the vendor: s3://redwood-pen-tests/1769801234/trace.log
Sara Patel: Audit gaps + externally routable internal endpoint = comp risk. vendor marked as HIGH. our initial triage team marked MEDIUM because keys weren't exported. we need to decide. @Maya Rivera your take for compliance?
Maya Rivera: from a compliance perspective, if the control plane leaked metadata and audit trails are incomplete, that edges toward HIGH. auditors care about ability to map keys to workloads.
Ben Morales: technical mitigation options: 1) tighten proxy ACL to deny non-admin accounts to /v1/keys, 2) add IAM check on control-plane side, 3) force inclusion of `x-audit-id` header and block if missing, 4) reingest missing audit events and surface alerts. timeline for quick patch (proxy ACL): ~3h.
Jay Chen: I also saw the control-plane returned `x-server-src: cplane-legacy` on those responses — sounds like an old codepath. might be leftover endpoint from migration.
Sara Patel: ok action items: Ben to push ACL change to prod, Jay to collect full request/response traces and timestamp ranges, Maya to prepare compliance rationale for escalation, Sara to coordinate vendor retest. Ben can you confirm ETA?
Ben Morales: starting ACL patch now. will create a canary rule, push to proxy-prod-02, monitor 15m, then roll. ETA 2.5h incl. smoke tests.
AuditBot: Incident created INC-2026-221 — \"KMS alias enumeration (pen test)\"; severity: UNASSIGNED; assignees: eng-security.
Jay Chen: attaching the relevant snippet from trace.log (redacted):
```
GET /v1/keys?aliasSearch=true HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-internal.com
Authorization: Bearer redacted_token
User-Agent: pen-test-client/1.2
Response: 200 OK
Body: {"aliases":["payments-prod-key","logs-rotation-key",...]}
```
Maya Rivera: also request CloudTrail/ControlPlane logs for 2026-03-12 10:00-10:30. need to confirm whether events were suppressed or never generated.
Sara Patel: I ran the staging retest after a config change — cannot reproduce in staging. vendor wants a retest in prod and their report insists on HIGH until verified.
Ben Morales: ACL patch deployed to proxy-prod-02. initial checks: 403 for non-admin token, 200 for admin token. waiting on logs to confirm.
Jay Chen: retest from vendor completed at 1769801400 — they report enumeration no longer works on proxy-prod-02, but hit proxy-prod-01 where patch not yet rolled. vendor attached a screenshot.
Maya Rivera: we need full audit evidence before we close. request: show matching CloudTrail entries that include the failed 403s and the earlier successful 200s, plus KMS audit logs for the alias lookups.
Ben Morales: pulling CloudTrail now. snippet placed in the same s3 folder: s3://redwood-pen-tests/1769801234/cloudtrail_snippet.json
AuditBot: Retest requested from vendor — vendor notified (vendor@pentestco) on 2026-03-17.
Sara Patel: proposal: set severity TEMP-HIGH until vendor verifies. remediation: (A) remove public routing for /v1/keys from non-admins, (B) add explicit `kms.alias.lookup` audit event and alert, (C) retire cplane-legacy codepath in 2 weeks. I'll open a remediation epic and assign owners.
Jay Chen: +1. I'll add the traces and vendor evidence to the ticket PT-921 for handoff.
Maya Rivera: I disagree with marking resolved until vendor signs off. we should keep as active until external validation and 48h of logs show no anomalies.
Ben Morales: agreed — marking as \"fix-deployed, awaiting external retest & 48h observation\". I'll add dashboard alert for sudden alias-listing activity.
Sara Patel: noted. I'll update the pen-test tracker and email the vendor the timeline. thx team :thumbsup:
Jay Chen: thanks all — will follow up when PT-921 has evidence attached.
